text:
Alex: Heads-up — found an edge when canarying a regional model variant with our smart routing + fallback rules.
Morgan: quick summary? :eyes:
Alex: We scoped the AB rollout to 'tier:startup' in eu-west. Traffic ran into a capacity blip in eu-west-low and fell back to variant v2 in us-east. That bumped latency and cost for startup customers.
Ravi: So fallback crossed region and tier? That sounds wrong. We intended fallback to stay within the same tier and region where possible.
Lina: We currently treat fallback as a simple ordered list of compatible variants. No tier/region awareness baked into the chain.
Sam: Repro steps: canary config below (snip).
Sam: ```json
{
  "rollout": "canary",
  "scope": {"tier": "startup", "region": "eu-west"},
  "variant": "v2-eu-quant",
  "fallbacks": ["v2-eu-quant", "v2-global-fp16", "v1-legacy"]
}
```
Jen: The ambiguity: should fallbacks be evaluated with the same scope predicate? e.g., only consider fallbacks where scope matches tier+region, then broaden to cross-region, then cross-tier.
Ravi: IMO yes. We should enforce 'scoped fallback' by default to avoid silently escalating customers to higher-cost variants or changing SLAs.
Morgan: UX question: how do we expose this in Console? Operators need to see 'fallback exposure' per tier+region, not just global fallback counts.
Alex: Telemetry gap: our traces only tag model_variant, not 'resolved_scope' — so we can't tell whether a startup request in eu-west actually got a cross-tier fallback. Need extra tags: resolved_tier, resolved_region, fallback_reason.
Lina: +1 for telemetry tags. Also quota interaction — if eu-west pool hits quota, fallback should respect customer quota buckets. Right now we fall back ignoring per-tier reserved capacity which caused startup requests to consume burst capacity in dedicated pools.
Sam: Proposed API patch: add fallbackStrategy field with values ["scoped-first", "global-first"], and add fallbackSteps that can include predicates. Example below.
Sam: ```json
{
  "fallbackStrategy": "scoped-first",
  "fallbackSteps": [
    {"predicate": {"tier": "same", "region": "same"}, "variants": ["v2-eu-quant"]},
    {"predicate": {"tier": "same", "region": "any"}, "variants": ["v2-global-fp16"]},
    {"predicate": {"tier": "any", "region": "any"}, "variants": ["v1-legacy"]}
  ]
}
```
Jen: Nice. We also need quota-aware ordering: each step should optionally check reserved_capacity[tier,region] before selecting.
Ravi: Implementation note: routing runtime must short-circuit and stream telemetry when fallback steps are hit to avoid request duplication. Also ensure quota checks are atomic with selection to avoid races.
Morgan: Console: show a rollout view with a matrix: rows=tier, cols=region, cells show exposure %, fallbacks triggered, P50/P95 latency delta. Click a cell to expand the fallback chain and current quotas.
Alex: Ops ask: default behavior for existing rollouts? We should default to scoped-first for safety and surface the config diff in the rollout change log.
Lina: Rollout API semantics: changing fallbackStrategy mid-rollout should require a migration step (preview + confirm) — we don't want sudden traffic shifts.
Sam: I'll draft a spec and a small migration plan. Will include sample UI mock and telemetry events (tags and metric names).
deploy-bot: deploy pipeline:canary-config-checker ran: no syntactic errors.
Alex: Thanks. Tagging @platform-owners for visibility. :thumbsup:
